facts.name: Astilbe
facts.light: Part shade; soil must stay moist
facts.notes: The classic shade bloomer, with feathery plumes in early summer that dry and stand into winter. Water in dry spells or the leaves crisp.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Bleeding Heart article

companions.why: Contrasts nicely with Japanese painted fern; combines well with astilbes, bleeding heart and Heuchera.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Brunnera 'Jack Frost' article

companions.why: Combines well with astilbe, columbine and ferns; plant with wild ginger, Virginia bluebells, Jacob's ladder and wild geranium; mix with iris.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Goat's Beard article

companions.why: Combines well with hosta and ferns; eye-catching near dark-leaved Heuchera, Pulmonaria or Brunnera; a backdrop for dark astilbe.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Japanese Forest Grass article
